mechanism_narrative: Accelerating GDP growth, as measured by the year-over-year change in real GDP, signals a strengthening economy that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Yield curve inverts (10y-2y < 0) during the 60-day forward window, indicating a growth slowdown that negates the positive signal from accelerating GDP.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in industrial production (INDPRO) over a 3-month period signals a supply shock that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as companies struggle with input disruptions and rising costs.
failure_condition: SPX returns are positive in > 55% of 20-day windows following a 3-month INDPRO drop of > 2%, indicating the market is shrugging off the supply shock.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a weakening labor market and slowing consumer demand, which will depress S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as companies face lower sales and earnings.
failure_condition: Consumer confidence (UMCSENT) rises by > 5 points over the 60-day forward window, indicating the labor market weakening is temporary and not significantly impacting consumer behavior.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4.5% and rising, it signals a tightening monetary policy that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: SPX returns are positive in > 60% of 20-day windows when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and rising, indicating the market is not responding negatively to the higher rates.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) both show year-over-year declines of > 5%, it signals a broad-based demand slowdown that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending contracts.
failure_condition: Consumer sentiment (UMCSENT) rises by > 5 points over the 60-day forward window, indicating the demand slowdown is temporary and not significantly impacting consumer behavior.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) is above its 12-month moving average and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 5%, it signals a tight labor market and strong industrial activity that will support positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX returns are negative in > 40% of 20-day windows when INDPRO is above its 12-month MA and UNRATE is below 5%, indicating the market is not responding positively to the strong supply-side indicators.

mechanism_narrative: When the CPI (CPIAUCSL) is rising by > 3% year-over-year and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 2%, it signals an inflationary environment with loose monetary policy that will support positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as investors seek returns in risk assets.
failure_condition: Real yields on 10-year TIPS turn positive over the 60-day forward window, indicating a shift toward tighter financial conditions that negates the positive signal from high inflation and low rates.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4% and falling, and payroll employment (PAYEMS) is rising by > 1% year-over-year, it signals a very tight labor market that will support wage growth and consumer spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Average hourly earnings (AHETPI) growth slows by > 1pp over the 20-day forward window, indicating the tight labor market is not translating into wage growth that supports consumer spending.
